synopsis: FMEA, FMECA and FMEDA examine component failures, effects and severity; FMEDA additionally assesses detection and classifies failures as safe or dangerous and detected or undetected, feeding diagnostic coverage and PL, MPL and SIL probability calculations [f12097, f12098]. MOSH requires a supplier FMECA to define critical faults for collision prevention products, treats degraded sensing as a fault, and requires fail-to-safe within 500 milliseconds of detecting a critical fault [f2358, f2905, f12102, f15643]. FMEA or FMEDA are inputs to fault injection and robustness testing, alongside injectable interfaces, SIL/HIL benches and diagnostic requirements; FMEDA tells testers which faults to inject and which diagnostics must catch, and can be completed before a prototype arrives [f1010, f12103, f12104, f12105]. The illustrative radar power-connector open circuit is dangerous because it prevents detections and braking commands; heartbeat loss detects it within 500 milliseconds, followed by fail-to-safe, but the example does not separately quantify the post-detection transition time [f12099, f12100, f12102]. In the illustrative automatic-braking safety case, FMEDA combines with fault-injection results and software verification to support the required Machine Performance Level claim, rather than establishing that claim alone [f12244].
